note: Bugs from an HR-swarm study, AI-verified not human-confirmed. axon/* files are a HUMAN-ONLY kernel floor: plan them as ADVISORY findings-only PRs (no autofix). Verify each fix with a targeted test.

bugs.summary: R9 axon-write gate uses the wrong anchor: _is_axon_path passes `workspace` (=<repo>/workspace) to is_axon_path, so the classifier checks paths against the non-existent `<repo>/workspace/axon` instead of the real kernel dir `<repo>/axon`. Absolute (and `../axon/…`) writes to the kernel are not recognized as axon writes.

The undo-completion code (log append, success message, CLEAR, DONE) was misplaced INSIDE the dry-run guard block AFTER a DONE, so it is unreachable, and the undo path falls straight through into the full combine flow.

Dry-run guard is not nested under the target-phase IF; all real phase-merge side effects are nested inside the dry-run branch and placed after DONE, and the ELSE binds to the dry-run IF instead of the target-phase IF.
DONE(workflow-run) at the end of the PROMOTE MODE block is dedented to column 0, making it unconditional instead of scoped to the `IF promote-run ≠ ∅` guard.
Save Output invokes the translate program with the arg key `input:` instead of the required `source:`, so translate receives no content and hard-fails.
Actor-failure branch falls through to EVAL instead of skipping the iteration; its eval-result write is dead and EVAL runs on empty/FAIL input.
Scaffold template hardcodes DONE(dev-new) instead of DONE({W:dev-new-name}), so every new program created by dev-new terminates with the wrong program name.
FIND used where a filter is needed — only the first active/completed plan is ever captured, so the list under-reports.
The dry-run merge gate misses mutating ops written inline after an arrow because _MUTATING_OP is anchored to line-start, so an unguarded mutator that writes via `→ WRITE(...)` passes.

_GUARD.search matches the dry-run token inside a `#` comment (no comment stripping), so a mutator whose real executable guard was removed but whose descriptive comment still mentions W:code-dev-dry-run passes the gate despite unguarded writes.

`matches` operator with an invalid regex RHS raises re.error, which is neither ParseError nor EvalError and is never caught, crashing the CLI and any workflow-gate caller instead of returning the uniform error envelope.

Health score is read via kv-store with an L: key, which kv_store.py refuses and which no longer holds the value, so score is always None and self-care always reports health as unknown / needs-attention.
os.open() writes/truncations of protected subtrees bypass the write-barrier because os.open raises the 'open' audit event with mode=None, which _hook treats as a read and lets through.
The task=="all" branch clears W:active-plan but never clears W:plan-done-name / W:plan-done-task, leaving stale input pointers that shadow the active-plan fallback on the next invocation.

restore() takes the reversibility self-snapshot (which enforces the FIFO cap and can evict the oldest snapshot) BEFORE reading the chosen snapshot's bytes, so restoring the oldest snapshot while the .rollback dir is at cap deletes `chosen` and then crashes reading it.
next-conditional edges are never validated even though the tool's contract says they are, so dangling conditional edges pass the fail-closed gate.
_run_has_receipts matches receipts by undelimited substring `run {run_id}`, letting a forged run borrow a prefix-sibling run's committed receipts.
preflight() crashes with an uncaught ValueError when the routine is given as a relative path and the tool is run from within the ROOT tree.
The integrity gate is fail-OPEN: it reports ok:true / note 'blessed' for any routine program_integrity.py does not track, defeating the documented fail-closed guarantee.

A no-program drift trace flips from stable to diverged/halt after a single recorded tool, contradicting the documented 'gate returns stable until TTL' contract and re-introducing the auto-improve halt it was meant to prevent.

probe_smoke (the default probe for any ACTIVE tool without a specific probe) returns status ACTIVE even when the tool's `--help` exits non-zero or times out, so genuinely broken tools are reported healthy.

_doctrine_host_mirror() imports _axon_paths without adding tools/ to sys.path, so it silently no-ops in the sentinel-governed path (the primary path), never writing the host-side tamper-evidence mirror.
_canonical_checksum re-serializes str values via json.dumps, contradicting its documented 'hashed directly' contract, so verify never matches for file/jsonl-append targets

_is_anchored(t.lower()) lowercases the token before classification, which permanently defeats the CamelCase anchor branch (regex [a-z][A-Z] can never match a lowercased string), so CamelCase-only acceptance items are misclassified as non-anchored.

ramp_record binds `state, _ = _ramp_load(ws)`, discarding the integrity_ok flag, then _ramp_save re-signs the loaded state — laundering hand-written/tampered clean cycles into a validly-signed state and bypassing the fail-closed HMAC ramp gate that gates S-fix autonomy.

_EXEC_RE / _STORE_RE are applied to raw program text with no comment/doc-section/quote stripping, so an EXEC token mentioned in a comment or ## HELP example above the real STORE(W:active-program,...) triggers a spurious 'EXEC appears BEFORE STORE' violation.
_STORE_RE.search matches a STORE(W:active-program,...) that appears only inside a comment/example, so a program with a real EXEC but no real active-program store is treated as compliant.
_PHASE_LEDGER_RE.search matches a TOOL(phase-ledger, record, ...) mention that lives only in a comment/example, so a program that takes ownership but never actually records a phase passes the check.
_subcommands_of resolves the tool script by name (tools/<name>.py) instead of the REGISTRY 'script' field, so tools whose registry name != script filename never get their subcommands checked.

handle_line's TOOL branch invokes registered tools with run_script(script) and NO arguments, silently dropping the subcommand + flags captured in RE_TOOL group(2) (and the '→ STORE(...result)' target in groups 3-5).

_extract_redirect_targets requires whitespace/start `(?:^|\s)` immediately before the redirect operator, so a redirect with no space before `>` (`word>file`) is not extracted and its target is never R9-inspected.

The gate recognizes and strips a leading `cd` (in _command_head) but no stage re-bases subsequent path resolution to the changed cwd. Each split segment's paths are resolved against `workspace`, so a `cd <dir> && <write/delete>` relocates the real cwd while the protected-delete and R9 checks inspect the wrong base.
The run verdict is computed only from failed==0, ignoring pytest collection/import errors and the process returncode, so a broken suite reports PASS (fail-open green gate).
Assistant reply is never persisted to the chat file — the PERSIST append omits the `text` field
Changelog reads 02-prs.md as a table and filters col5="merged", but the file is authored as a bullet list whose status is stored as '- **Status:** ...' text, never a 'merged' table column.
The C8 dry-run guard is placed AFTER the mutating RESTORE-DIR it is meant to protect, so `--undo` under an armed dry-run still overwrites the phases/ tree.

SCAN builds the append shadow-path from the codebase-RELATIVE path, but `shadow init` created the file under the FULL absolute path convention (`_shadow_path_for` strips only the leading '/'), so the four appends target a non-existent file and silently no-op.
list branch passes the string '7d' to igap's integer-typed --days flag, crashing the default `code-dev meta igap` invocation.
Guard uses CONTAINS with a regex-anchored literal '^- ', so it never matches real bullets — _dont-do.md is always re-seeded and overwritten, clobbering existing prohibitions.
Botched semantic-search deprecation leaves search-results/arch-findings undefined but still STORE'd and dereferenced downstream.
shadow append is called with an unsupported --date flag, so the per-edit findings write crashes and is silently lost while the program reports success.
SESSION HOOK hardcodes state=frozen (and anchor=freeze) regardless of mode, so 'code-dev thaw' re-freezes the session at entry.
TOOL(shell, git branch) result is bound whole (envelope dict) without unwrapping .stdout, so branch-drift detection always false-positives and {git-branch} renders the raw envelope.
The `actions` subcommand is documented in usage, desc, and the FAIL message's own valid-list, but the CASE has no `actions` branch, so it falls through to the wildcard and fails.
In the flag-mode DISPATCH block, the 'PHASE NOT ADVANCED' escalation and human-handoff run unconditionally instead of only on outputs-missing, and the ELSE IF is dangling.
Phase subcommand dispatch reads unwritten key W:code-dev-phase-cmd instead of the parsed second token `sub`, so `code-dev phase list` runs code-dev-phase-new.

config wizard matches the autonomy decision with exact `≡` against short labels, but W:_decision holds the full option string, so the 'attended' branch is never taken and capabilities are granted fail-open.

The 'LOW fix' that surfaces dependency issues is dead: `issues` is referenced at line 32 before it is initialized, and line 37 (`issues ← []`) unconditionally re-initializes the list, discarding whatever line 32 appended.
The report tool is invoked with an undefined variable `findings-json`, so the cycle report is written with no finding data.
`versions` reads W:_versions-target, which no code path writes, and (unlike its siblings simulate.md/library-dev.md) lacks the W:_arg1 fallback — so the CLI target argument is always ignored.

_write_receipt records the tool name as typed (sys.argv[1], possibly an alias) without resolving it to its canonical registry name, so R_TOOL_RECEIPTS mismatches claims that reference the canonical name.
Interrupt-gate ABORT branch clears W:_interrupt-pending-input on line 258, then tries to EXEC that same (now-empty) key on line 260, so the user's new action is silently dropped on abort.

Interrupt gate binds 'answer <- input' from the SAME input that triggered the interrupt, not from the K/I/A reply, so none of the K/I/A handler branches (lines 243/246/254) can execute on the prompt turn; and because the gate re-fires on EVERY input before parsing (line 208), the K/I/A reply on the next turn re-enters the ELSE branch and overwrites W:_interrupt-pending-input.
Slack alert message interpolates {W:batch-key}, a memory key that is never stored.
RAND(W:batch, W:sample-size) misuses RAND — there is no 'sample N without replacement' form.
OUTPUT section interpolates W:pref-topic/pref-key/pref-value after they were CLEARed three lines earlier, so the user-facing confirmation renders with blank fields.

In-process usage_record writes ts as isoformat()+"Z" ("...+00:00Z"), which usage.py's readers cannot parse with datetime.fromisoformat, so those entries are silently dropped from all windowed queries.

clock's `unix` field is computed with naive-UTC `.timestamp()`, which Python interprets as LOCAL time, so `unix` is wrong (off by the host's UTC offset) on any non-UTC machine while iso/date/time stay correct.
The sentinel-seam caller pattern r'\bauthorized\s*\(' for autonomous_mode.authorized matches unrelated English prose, so a genuinely-dead governance seam is reported as wired.
`in` operator guards the RHS type but not LHS/RHS compatibility: `<non-string> in <string>` raises TypeError, which is not caught by main()'s (ParseError, EvalError) handler and crashes.
main() calls args.func(args) but never propagates the function's return value to sys.exit, so cmd_generate/cmd_query/cmd_validate's `return 1` error paths exit 0.

Reported hit start/end offsets are relative to the progressively-redacted string, not the original text, so hits from any pattern after the first are misreported when an earlier pattern replaced text of a different length (contradicts the line-27 'original positions' contract).
Dead-rule detection uses substring containment (`r["id"] not in log_text`), so a rule id that is a prefix of another (R-1 vs R-10) is falsely counted as referenced and never flagged dead.
complete-claim check uses a substring test `"complete" in (status+" "+phase)`, which matches the substring inside 'incomplete', producing a false complete-claim-unbacked finding.

Data source is selected with a truthiness test (`if args.data`) instead of a None check, so an empty `--data ''` falls through to `open(args.data_file)` with args.data_file=None, raising an uncaught TypeError.
repo_sha is computed against the git-archive checkout (which has no .git), so every record's provenance field is always "unknown".
_OPEN_RE only captures the first quoted string in open(), so raw writes with a literal path argument (mode is the 2nd string) are never detected, defeating the R9 immutability gate.
C3 'unclassified' menu-coverage check is unreachable because programs_registry._menu_category never returns a falsy value.
resolve_limit() discards an explicit --limit that happens to equal DEFAULT_LIMIT (128000), overriding it with the host-model window and violating the documented 'explicit --limit wins' precedence.
Dependency scanner skips markdown table rows, so programs that dispatch via a routing table have their real EXEC() deps dropped; the dep checker then reports 'ok' even for broken/missing routes.

Feedback auto-tune reports `threshold_adjusted` even when the change is never persisted, because the re.sub of `dispatch-confidence:` silently no-ops when that line is absent (and the write is skipped entirely if the pref file is missing).
Conformance gate uses naive substring matching instead of checking for real STORE(L:...) declarations, so a required capability key mentioned only in a comment satisfies the gate.

append_table_row inserts `\n{row}` at the offset AFTER the last table row's trailing newline and appends no trailing newline of its own. When the table's last row is immediately followed by another line (e.g. a `## SECTION` header), the new row is concatenated onto that following line, destroying it; it also injects a spurious blank line splitting the table.
get reports a legitimately-stored JSON null value as not-found, contradicting exists
cmd_gc rewrites the ledger without re-chaining prev-sha, so any GC removal makes verify_chain report a false tamper break on an untampered ledger

L: rollback can only ever reach the single most-recent prior value; older stored history entries (up to ROLLBACK_MAX-1) are permanently unreachable, so repeated rollback oscillates instead of walking back through history.

export_fresh's 'unchanged' fast-path reports notes/edges from the raw graph (symbol-node count and total-link count) instead of the file-note count and cross-file-edge count that build_vault actually produces, so identical re-invocations return wildly different, wrong counts.
ARITH_RE fails open on percent and currency arithmetic — exactly the 'money/%' cases the BLOCK rule names — because '%' is in the operator class and the right operand must begin with a bare digit.
parse_dont_do does not reset `cur` when a disabled (~~struck~~) bullet is encountered, so the disabled bullet's indented match:/review: line clobbers the previous active prohibition's token.

_STORE_RE over-matches: `STORE\(\s*L:inference-mode\b` also matches longer keys like L:inference-mode-locked (the lock-control key) and any L:inference-mode-<suffix>, because \b matches at the '-' boundary and [^)]* then swallows '-locked, ...'.
_CLAIM_RE's dispatcher-CLI branch (axon.py <token>) captures non-tool subcommands like 'help', which can never be receipted, causing a fail-closed false BLOCK when tool-receipts mode is on.
Promoted `.draft.yml` files (documented 'never auto-activated') are enumerated as installed workflows and shadow the active workflow of the same name in resolve/sub-workflow loading.
resolve_next silently drops a rule whose `if:` is a boolean true (unquoted YAML), the opposite of its stated semantics.
notes-dir uses `{project.path}` but W:code-dev-project is a slug string, not an object with a .path field.
`{coverage-pct}` is interpolated in the GAP AREAS output but the variable is never assigned anywhere in the program.
The required-args guard `if not all([args.workflow, args.src_tokens, args.cmp_tokens])` treats a legitimately-provided value of 0 as 'missing' because 0 is falsy.

load_log identifies header/separator rows by substring (`'Date' not in line`, `'---' not in line`), so any recorded data row whose workflow (or other column) contains those substrings is silently dropped from `list` and `stats`.

The user prompt is passed as the argparse option value '--value <prompt>'; when the stripped prompt is a single option-like token (e.g. '-h', '--foo', '-v') memory.py/prompt_log/anticipate reject it and all three actions silently no-op.

declared_subs() takes the LAST {a,b,c} group in the usage line as the subcommand set; for a subparser-less tool whose only {...} group is an option's choices (e.g. --format {json,text}), it returns those choices as if they were subcommands, causing a false unknown-subcommand violation.
cmd_reconcile records the fix result into res['fix_applied'] and then immediately rebinds `res` to a fresh reconcile() dict, discarding the fix report from all output.
Empty --text input is treated as absent and falls through to the file branch, crashing on args.files=None.
